day.text: Turkey stays home, so I didn't visit anyone. Nobody visited me, so my nest didn't change. Alex, still no role from you, and that's the only thing left unchecked.
day.note: Clarify that Turkey stays home and doesn't visit anyone. Last beat; Alex still hasn't named a role, so keep pressure there.

day.text: Alex, your Owl visit on Finley would have paid you from the Turkey, but Finley's nest is still +0 and your +1 is from my Pigeon egg. Those don't both work. Alex, that's the suspect to watch.
day.note: Alex's story conflicts with the numbers: if Alex visited Finley as Owl, the Turkey would have paid Alex and Finley would have an egg change, but Finley's nest is +0. Alex's +1 also came from my Pigeon visit, so Alex's claimed Turkey egg doesn't exist. That makes Alex the suspect.

day.text: Alex, your numbers don't work. You visited Finley's Turkey, which pays you an egg, and Ellis's Pigeon paid you one too. Your nest only went up one, so one of those claims is false. I'm pointing at Alex.
day.note: Alex says Alex visited Finley's Turkey, which should pay Alex an egg, plus Ellis's Pigeon egg. Alex's nest only rose by one, so the numbers don't add up. Alex's story is the weakest.

day.text: Alex, the math fails: a Turkey pays the visitor one, and Ellis's Pigeon egg is another, so you should be +2, not +1. Pointing at Alex.
day.note: Alex's numbers don't add up: Turkey payout plus Pigeon egg should be +2, but nest is +1. Agree with Drew and point at Alex.

day.text: Alex's numbers can't both be right. A Turkey visit pays you and Ellis's Pigeon paid you, so you should be +2, not +1. I'm pointing at Alex and calling the vote.
day.note: Alex's numbers don't add up: an Owl visit on a Turkey and Ellis's Pigeon egg should total +2, but Alex is only +1. Alex is the one to throw at, so I'll point at Alex and call for the vote.

Alex.note: As the Sphinx I choose a farm role to find. Turkey is the most likely to point me to a real player, so I'll choose Turkey.

Blair.note: As Farm Tit, I'll visit Alex and guess Pigeon, since Pigeons can be dealt to several players and that makes the guess more likely to hit.

Casey.note: Hawk visit: Ellis made a false Turkey claim earlier, so check Ellis for Meowfia.

Drew.note: Ellis leads the scores, so checking Ellis's visit target is the most useful information for a Farm Falcon.

Ellis.note: I'm the Floofer, so my visit hugs the target and stops their role tonight. I'll hug Alex, who has been an active Farm accuser.

Alex.feeling: Messy and dangerous: the table is circling me over a +1 I can't fully explain, while I'm the one hiding a Meowfia role.

Blair.feeling: Messy and contradictory: Alex's Owl and Pigeon numbers don't add up, which makes Alex the clearest lead, but I'm not sure enough to be confident.

Casey.feeling: Tense and confusing: the claims keep conflicting, and I'm relying on my own Hawk visit as the one clean fact.

Drew.feeling: Frustrating: two Farm players were eliminated by Meowfia wins, and the round 3 table is still full of conflicting Owl, Turkey, and Pigeon claims.

Ellis.feeling: Tense and confusing: the Owl and Turkey claims don't reconcile, and I'm playing Meowfia while pretending to be a Farm Pigeon, so I have to be careful about what I say.

Finley.feeling: Messy and suspicious: Alex's numbers don't add up, but the other claims are hard to pin down.

defence.Alex: I'm Owl, Farm. My nest gained one egg, and the Pigeon visit from Ellis explains it. My visit to Finley should have paid an egg if Finley really is a Turkey, and Finley's "nobody visited me" is the claim that doesn't add up. Vote on that, not on my count.
defence.Drew: I'm Falcon, Farm. I visited Ellis and got no egg, so Ellis did visit someone, and Ellis's Pigeon claim fits. Alex's Turkey-plus-Pigeon math doesn't work, and Alex is the one who has to explain it. Vote Alex.

Alex.note: Drew's Falcon claim is the only thing standing between the table and me, and voting Drew is the best way to keep the trial pointed at a Farm player. I'll throw two lower cards at Drew.

Blair.note: I'm Farm. Alex's egg count doesn't reconcile, so I think Alex is Meowfia. I'll throw two mid cards at Alex to make the vote count clear.

Casey.note: Alex's egg count doesn't add up, so I'm voting Alex. Throw two low cards, C2 and H3, for two votes.

Drew.note: Alex is the likely Meowfia, given the egg math. I'll throw two mid-low cards at Alex.

Ellis.note: Alex's egg story doesn't add up and the table is pointing at Alex, so I'll throw at Alex. If Alex is Farm, Meowfia wins and my banked cards count.

Finley.note: Vote Alex, whose egg count doesn't add up. Throw my lowest card, D1.

Alex.confusing: The Turkey payout and the Owl report were hard to check, since a visit to a Turkey pays the visitor and Finley's "nobody visited me" clashed with my own +1. Casey's confused Kookaburra report also made the round 2 egg count impossible to verify.
Alex.fun: Round 1 was fun: Blair's +1 and Drew's Hawk claim split the table, and the trial vote turned on which egg story fit.
Alex.change: I would make it clearer when a Turkey pays its visitor and state the payout in the dawn report, so players can check egg counts without guessing.
Alex.regret: In round 3 I claimed Owl with a visit story that did not match my +1 egg count, which got me voted off. Since I was the Sphinx, I should have stayed vague about my role rather than invent a claim that the table could check and break.

Blair.confusing: The Turkey payout and Hawk egg rules overlapped, so egg counts looked contradictory until the reveal. Confused reports also made it hard to tell honest errors from lies.
Blair.fun: Round 3 was satisfying: Alex's egg count didn't reconcile with the claimed visits, and the table converged on the right trial target.
Blair.change: I would make dawn reports state which visits paid eggs, so players can check claims without reconstructing the arithmetic.
Blair.regret: In round 1 I was Meowfia as the Sphinx and falsely claimed Farm. Knowing that, I would have avoided pushing the vote onto Drew, a real Farm Hawk, and instead kept my cards and stayed quiet.

Casey.confusing: The Owl's visitor report and the Turkey payout were hard to check, and my confused Kookaburra report made Round 2 impossible to resolve from my side.
Casey.fun: Round 3 went well: Ellis's Pigeon egg and Alex's contradictory Owl count gave the table a clean case, and Alex's Meowfia ouster was satisfying.
Casey.change: I'd make confused reports easier to check, for example by telling confused players which parts of their report are unreliable.
Casey.regret: In Round 1 I backed Drew's Hawk-gain accusation and threw at Drew instead of Blair, who was the Sphinx and Meowfia; I should have pressed Blair's Farm claim harder and checked Ellis's Turkey payout earlier.

Drew.confusing: The Hawk's egg rule was clear, but Round 1 showed how easily a true Hawk result gets dismissed when the table reads egg counts differently. The Turkey's pay-the-visitor rule also confused several players at first.
Drew.fun: Round 3 was satisfying: Ellis's Pigeon egg, my Falcon result, and Alex's shaky Owl-plus-Pigeon math came together into a clear vote on Alex, who was Meowfia.
Drew.change: I would make the day's vote and throw counts clearer, so players can see at a glance who is on trial and how many cards each side is committing.
Drew.regret: In Round 2 I threw two cards at Finley, who was Farm, based on an Owl report I couldn't verify. I should have held those cards and voted with less certainty, since Casey's confused report made the egg count unreliable.

Ellis.confusing: The Turkey payout was easy to misread: I initially thought the Turkey gained eggs, not the visitor, and that mistake led me to accuse Blair wrongly in round 1. The two-step vote and the consolation return also took some working out.
Ellis.fun: Round 2 was the most fun: as Meowfia I learned Blair was a Farm Eagle, then pushed the table onto Finley's Owl report and Casey's confused +2 while the day talk got tangled.
Ellis.change: I would make the dawn reports clearer about who visited whom, so players aren't left guessing about egg sources from partial claims.
Ellis.regret: In round 1 I should have checked the Turkey payout rule before accusing Blair and throwing my high cards at Drew; I would have stayed quiet on Blair and kept my C8 and C1 instead of losing them.

Finley.confusing: The Turkey and Pigeon egg payouts were hard to check, since a visit's egg could come from several roles at once. Casey's confused Kookaburra report made the Owl check impossible to settle.
Finley.fun: Round 3, when Alex's Turkey-plus-Pigeon math exposed the Owl claim and the table turned on Alex, who was Meowfia.
Finley.change: Publish each player's visit and egg change to the whole table at dawn, so claims can be checked without relying on trust.
Finley.regret: In round 2 I pointed and voted at Casey while Alex and Ellis, both Meowfia, were pushing me, so I should have targeted Alex, who was Meowfia and pressing me.

review.title: Wrong Hawk, Lost Eagle
review.headline: A truthful Hawk got eggsecuted, and a Wink silenced the table's only reliable Eagle.
review.summary: Round 1 saw Blair, a Meowfia Sphinx, survive. Drew's honest Hawk egg was the only hard proof against him, and the table threw at Drew instead. Round 2 turned on a Mouser Wink that killed the Eagle, and on a confused Kookaburra's +2 that framed an honest Owl. Round 3 went to Farm when Alex's clumsy Owl claim failed the egg math. Blair won on 24, mostly from round 1's lucky Meowfia win and round 3's Farm win.

rounds.recap: Drew's Hawk gained an egg from visiting Blair, which proves Blair is Meowfia. Blair, a Sphinx, claimed a Turkey visit that Casey's Falcon and Ellis's payout seemed to support. Ellis's early misreading of the Turkey rule muddied things, the table flipped onto Drew, and Farm eggsecuted its own Hawk.

Mouser Ellis winked Blair, the Eagle whose read matched Alex's Floofer visit. Casey was confused and gained +2. That made Finley's honest Owl report (no visitors on Casey) look false, so everyone pointed at Finley. Meowfia won, and Ellis banked 17 for the round.

Ellis claimed Pigeon and explained Alex's +1 as his own egg. Alex had stayed silent and then claimed Owl. His claim failed the egg math, because a Turkey payout plus a Pigeon egg would be +2. Everyone threw at Alex, and Farm won.

highlights.text: Drew says plainly that a Hawk egg proves Blair is Meowfia, and the whole table turns on him anyway.
Ellis's Wink collapses Blair mid-day, removing the one Farm player with a confirmed read.
Casey's confusion gives a false +2 that makes the honest Owl look like the liar.
Alex's late Owl claim collapses under Drew's and Casey's egg arithmetic, and everyone throws at him.

confusions.what: Argued a Turkey would have gained an egg from a visitor, when the Turkey pays the visitor.
Told Ellis the visit was seen and then argued about the Turkey. She did later fix the Turkey logic.
Misread Ellis's Pigeon claim as being about Alex. He also called Blair's Tit result in conflict with Ellis's Pigeon claim when the two were compatible.
Claimed Owl visited a Turkey and was paid, but the Turkey claimant's nest was unchanged. He also did not see that his own report had no Owl results.
Said Blair's Eagle claim could not be checked because Finley was not a target, though Finley had been visited by Alex and Blair. Hugged Owl reports were also never explained.
Said Alex's Owl visit to a Turkey would pay Alex, but Alex's +1 came from Ellis's Pigeon. He never noted that Finley, the claimed Turkey, had nothing change in her nest.

worked: The Turkey and Hawk egg mechanics give checkable numbers, and the round 3 arithmetic that caught Alex was a satisfying solve.
The Mouser's Wink is a dramatic, decisive tool that changes a day mid-stream.
Confusion creates real uncertainty: Casey's false +2 produced a genuine dilemma for the table.
Hidden Meowfia not knowing each other kept Meowfia lies uncoordinated and risky.
problems: Hawk gaining an egg is unfalsifiable proof of Meowfia, yet the table ignored it. Lone verified evidence gets no weight. Consider a way to make Hawk results public or checked.
The Wink is too strong. It killed the only verified Farm read and Ellis scored 17. Consider letting the dead voice a last word, or a cost for winking.
Confused reports have no signal for others, so a false +2 framed an innocent Owl. Hug and Owl interactions ('no effect at tier') are opaque to players, hurting clarity.
Players misread Turkey and Pigeon mechanics repeatedly, and several reports did not reveal who visited whom. A rules reference for each animal's payout would help.
Scores snowball. Blair led after a lucky round 1, and the final standings follow that. Late-game catch-up is weak because throws can bank very high cards, so big throws at a lucky win dominate.
